discovery: Production and quantum control of ultracold molecules: buffer-gas and direct laser cooling of molecules and the creation of quantum-degenerate polar molecular gases

nominees.name: Jun Ye
nominees.affiliation: JILA, NIST and University of Colorado Boulder, USA

nominees.name: David DeMille
nominees.affiliation: University of Chicago and Argonne National Laboratory, USA

motivation: Molecules, with their rich internal structure and permanent dipole moments, long resisted the cooling methods that transformed atomic physics. The nominees overcame this. Doyle invented cryogenic buffer-gas cooling and beams, a general source of cold molecules, and with DeMille established direct laser cooling and magneto-optical trapping of molecules (SrF, CaF), later extended to polyatomics in tweezer arrays. Ye, building on the KRb work with the late Deborah Jin, created ultracold ground-state polar molecules, observed dipolar quantum chemistry and spin-exchange physics, and reached a degenerate Fermi gas of polar molecules. Together these advances turned molecules into fully controllable quantum systems. They enable quantum simulation with long-range interactions, state-to-state ultracold chemistry, new qubit platforms, and precision tests of fundamental symmetries, notably the ACME electron EDM bounds and JILA's ion-based EDM measurements, which probe physics beyond the Standard Model. This creates a new field that spans physics and chemistry.
